claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. 

To get started, I'll need to gather some information about your situation. Let me ask you the first question:

**What is the name of the child (or children) you're inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm inquiring about my son Alex. He's 13 years old and lives with me here in the UK. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So I'm assessing eligibility for **Alex**, your 13-year-old son who lives with you in the UK.

Before I can determine your eligibility, I need to check a few more important details about your circumstances.

**Are you a British citizen, EEA citizen, or do you have settled status in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm a British citizen and I live here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that. That's helpful information.

Now I need to check a few more details about Alex's situation:

**Is Alex in full-time education, apprenticeship, or approved training?** (Or if he's not, what is his current situation?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's just in regular secondary school. He's only 13, so just doing his normal school years - nothing special like college or training yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Just to make sure I have the right understanding:

**When you say he's in "regular secondary school," you mean he attends school as a full-time student, correct?** (In other words, he's in compulsory education at a standard secondary school?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - he's in compulsory education at a regular secondary school. He goes to school full-time like any other 13-year-old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for confirming that. I have most of the information I need now.

Just one more important question:

**Has Alex ever been in local authority care, or is he currently receiving any benefits in his own name (such as Disability Living Allowance or Personal Independence Payment)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's never been in care, and he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a regular kid living at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent, thank you for that information. I now have all the details I need to assess your eligibility. Let me review the Child Benefit eligibility rules to make my determination.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Based on the information you've provided and the Child Benefit eligibility rules I've reviewed, I can now provide you with my determination:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news!** You are **eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Your situation meets all the eligibility requirements:
- You're a British citizen living in the UK
- Alex is 13 years old (under 16)
- He lives with you
- He's in full-time education at secondary school
- He has never been in local authority care
- He doesn't receive any benefits in his own name

You should now be able to make a claim with HMRC. If you have any further questions about your eligibility or need more information, you can contact the Child Benefit Office.

Therefore, you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.
